title: INTERNET ECON, ENG ＆ SOCIETY
description: Mathematical models, analyses of economics and networking interdependencies in the internet. Topics include microeconomics of pricing and regulations in communications industry, game theory in revenue allocations, ISP settlements, network externalities, two-sided markets. Economic principles in networking and network design, decentralized vs. centralized resource allocation, “price of anarchy,” congestion control. Case studies of topical internet issues. Societal and industry implications of internet evolution.
prerequisites_text: Prerequisites: ( CSEE W4119 ) or ( ELEN E6761 ) CSEE W4119 or ELEN E6761 recommended, and ability to comprehend and track development of sophisticated models.
